Senses.PreferredTarget: Yangshan tipped out a whole basketful
AlternateTargets: Yangshan poured out an entire basket
SearchAliases: Yangshan poured out an entire basket
Senses.Explanation: “Yangshan tipped out a whole basketful” answers the East Temple’s request for one sea-calming pearl by multiplying the requested treasure. Foyan Qingyuan reports his own realization of this answer after Yuanwu Keqin pressed the contradiction in Yangshan’s pearl case. Zhongfeng Mingben sets the basketful beside a shout and a whole canon and asks whether such words are rubble or treasure. Tian’an Sheng raises the pearl case, distinguishes pearl from rubble, and calls Yangshan’s basketful an enhancement of the Chan seat. Wuyi Yuanlai places the answer in verse and asks for the mind that is originally buddha.
Senses.Note: Bind the basketful to the East Temple’s request for the sea-calming pearl. A generic basket or act of pouring is not this case label.

Senses.Explanation: “Yangshan asks Zhongyi” labels the encounter in which Yangshan Huiji asks Zhongyi Hong’en about buddha-nature. Zhongyi compares a room with six windows and a monkey inside answering calls from outside. Yangshan then asks how the outside monkey can meet it when the inner monkey sleeps; Zhongyi comes down, grasps Yangshan, and says they have met. Hongzhi Zhengjue verses the sleeping monkey and the reopening of spring. Wansong Xingxiu emphasizes Yangshan’s counter-question after the easy explanation. Dahui Zonggao and Yulin Tongxiu each raise the case in live exchanges and add their own tests. Poshan Haiming also raises the case, criticizes Zhongyi for naming buddha-nature and monkey, and adds a verse.
Senses.Note: Treat this as a case label. The six-window monkey is Zhongyi’s analogy; Yangshan’s sleeping-monkey question turns the encounter.

Senses.Explanation: “Yangshan plants the hoe” is the case label for Yangshan setting down his hoe and standing with folded hands after Guishan asks how many people are in the fields. Foyan Qingyuan’s verse section uses the label and verses the difficulty of the clearly stated number. Wansong Xingxiu raises the whole exchange and comments on the teacher and student meeting. Wuzhun Shifan gives the label a separate verse, while Linquan Conglun raises and comments on the case together with later judgments by Xuansha and Jingqing.
Senses.Note: Bind the label to Guishan’s field question, Yangshan’s folded-hands stance, and his later lifting the hoe and leaving. It is not generic farm work.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase “When tired, sleep” forms the second half of the hunger-and-sleep saying, and Dazhu’s case explicitly distinguishes this from sleeping while occupied by calculations. When tired, sleep. Its stable partner is ‘when hungry, eat’. In the Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, the Vinaya master Youyuan asks Dazhu Huihai whether he exerts effort in following the Way. Dazhu says yes and answers with eating when hungry and sleeping when tired. When Youyuan objects that everyone does the same, Dazhu says they differ: while eating, others do not consent simply to eat but make a hundred demands; while sleeping, they do not consent simply to sleep but make a thousand calculations. A song attributed to Nanyue Lanzan places the pair after refusing delight in heaven or merit-making and before saying fools laugh while the wise understand. The words remain ordinary bodily actions; the recorded public exchange contrasts Dazhu’s stated exertion with the same-looking conduct accompanied by demands and calculation.

Senses.Explanation: Within the realm the emperor's edict governs; beyond the frontier the general's command does. Donglin Yan, Cuiyan Kezhen, Yuan'an Liao's questioner, and Chulin Shangrui use that division in cases about speaking and silence, commands taking effect, and Nanquan's uncompromising acts. Donglin Yan gives the pair after raising Fengxue's answer about passing through speech and silence. Cuiyan Kezhen uses it while distinguishing Xuefeng's handling from his own. An unnamed questioner presents it to Yuan'an Liao as the frame for asking when a tally arrives and an order takes effect. Chulin Shangrui verses it after Nanquan's actions.
